languages.name: Dibiyaso
sources: Reesink (1976) - comparative notes and 97 terms for Bainapi
Rueck, MacKenzie & Alemán (2005) - 156 terms for Dibiyaso of Bamustu, Makapa, Pikiwa
Franklin & Voorhoeve (1973) - 47 comparative terms for Bainapi
languages.notes: 3 villages only; each village has different name for language (Turumasa in Makapa, Bainapi in Pikiwa, Dibiasu in Bamustu)

languages.name: Guriaso
sources: Baron (1983) Kwomtari Survey - 1979 census data for 5 villages
languages.notes: Also called Muno; 5 main villages + 1 switching village; 1979 census: 347 resident, 74 absent = 421 total

languages.name: Karami
sources: Flint (1919:96) - only existing wordlist recorded Oct 12, 1917
languages.notes: Extinct; only 2 villages documented; only a short wordlist survives with many Foia Foia loans

languages.name: Kehu
languages.province: Papua Province, Nabire Regency, Wapoga District
languages.notes: NOT in Papua New Guinea - in Indonesia (Papua province); also called Keuw; single village

languages.name: Komolom (Mombum)
languages.province: South Papua, Merauke Regency, Kimaam District
sources: Wikipedia (Mombum language, Komoran Island) / Ethnologue / Glottolog
Joshua Project / Linguistic Diversity at Risk (2024)
languages.notes: NOT in Papua New Guinea - in Indonesia (South Papua); single village on Komolom Island; also called Mombum/Kemelom

languages.name: Komyandaret
languages.province: South Papua, Boven Digoel Regency, Firiwage District
sources: de Vries (2012) - Tsaukambo language notes mentioning Komyandaret
languages.notes: NOT in Papua New Guinea - in Indonesia (South Papua); 60% lexical similarity with Tsaukambo; likely dialect continuum

languages.name: Konai
languages.province: Western Province (Murray River area, west of Strickland River)
sources: Årsjö & Årsjö (2005) - Phonology and orthography essentials, SIL
Årsjö & Årsjö (1991, 2000) - Sociolinguistic survey and field notes
languages.notes: 9 villages total (7 major + 2 Eastern dialect); 3 dialects: Lowland, Foothill, Mountain; villages spread over 30-35km

languages.name: Koneraw
languages.province: South Papua, Merauke Regency, Yos Sudarso (Kolopom) Island
verified_toponyms: Single village on south coast of Kolopom/Yos Sudarso Island (Konorau)
languages.notes: NOT in Papua New Guinea - in Indonesia (South Papua); single village surrounded by Kimaghama speakers; sister language to Mombum

languages.name: Kubo
verified_toponyms: Gwaimasi (= Komagato) - on Gwai stream, west bank Strickland River
Mome Hafi (junction of Mome and Dege streams)
Dege Hafi (junction of Dege stream and Strickland River)
Tagohai / Tobi 2 / Molo Village (junction of Molo and Dogomo River)
Suwa'a 2, Hima'a, Biya'a, Gobamo'o, Diyo'o (streams/clan boundaries)
Forbidden place (toin sa) near Sasosi Village
Sacred site (rock with human face imprint) near Sasosi
sources: Minnegal & Dwyer 'Navigating the Future' (ANU Press 2017) - detailed toponyms
'Where all the rivers flow west' (2014) - maps with named sites
PNG NRI Discussion Paper 214 (2023) - Kubo/Febi migration to Kiunga
Wikipedia / Ethnologue / Glottolog (kubo1242) / Joshua Project / TransNewGuinea.org
languages.notes: Rich toponymic landscape documented by Dwyer & Minnegal over 30 years; named streams, swamps, mountains, caves, sacred sites, clan land boundaries; likely 50+ toponyms in ethnographic record

kula_note: Kula (ISO: tpg, not kls) is in INDONESIA (Alor Island), NOT Papua New Guinea. It has 31 documented toponyms from 2023-2026 fieldwork (Perono Cacciafoco et al.) and CAN reach 25+. kls = Kalasha (Pakistan).
kawacha_note: kcb = Kawacha (PNG, Huon Peninsula, ~1,000 speakers) - different language from Kubo (jko).
